evidence: The $SP alternation matches Go's unicode.IsSpace set: ASCII \t\n\v\f\r and space, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F and U+3000.
The lead bytes \xc2, \xe1, \xe2 and \xe3 are never continuation bytes (0x80-0xBF), so a trim cannot start in the middle of another valid character.
The text stays a byte string with no utf8 flag after utf8::decode and utf8::encode were removed, so the \x80-\xff escapes in the regex match single bytes.
The project key match `\Aproject$SP*:` and the value trims are consistent with the previous behaviour on valid UTF-8 input.
The perl program is inside single quotes and the new code adds no single quote, so shell quoting is intact.
